html:
In April 1767 the armies of the Burmese Konbaung dynasty took Ayutthaya after a siege of over a year, ending the kingdom of Ayutthaya.

The city was burned, its temples looted and tens of thousands of people carried off to Burma, including members of the royal family, artists and scholars. The last king died during the fall.

China then attacked Burma, and the Burmese withdrew most troops. The general Taksin rallied the Siamese, drove out the remaining Burmese and made Thonburi his capital. His successor founded Bangkok in 1782. Ayutthaya's ruins, such as Wat Chaiwatthanaram, remain. See Alaungpaya.
sum: In April 1767 the armies of the Burmese Konbaung dynasty took Ayutthaya after a siege of over a year, ending the kingdom of Ayutthaya.
